root_causes.root_cause: Docling TableFormer renders checkmark/symbol-only PDF cells as empty strings because rasterized glyphs have no text layer and tiny icons defeat OCR. RFC-010 Gap 6b documents this as an upstream limitation with mitigation via empty_cell_ratio/suspected_miss flagging already shipped in flag_empty_cells().
root_causes.suggested_fix: Symbol-cell recovery requires either (a) per-cell OCR fallback on empty cells that neighbor non-empty cells in the same table, or (b) a VLM-based table re-extraction pass for tables with empty_cell_ratio > threshold. Both are outside the current Docling pipeline. RFC-010 Gap 6b already documents this as unfixable at the pageindex layer.

root_causes.root_cause: Chart-image OCR produces fragmented single-token numeric labels that the flat block parser (route_and_extract_flat) classifies as individual kv/prose blocks instead of structured table/series data. The splice_picture_text_for_tree function appends raw OCR text after image markers but has no chart-data structuring logic. No code change caused this -- it is a persistent limitation of OCR-to-flat-block conversion for chart images.
root_causes.suggested_fix: Chart-aware post-processing: after OCR extraction, detect chart-like numeric token sequences and group them into structured table blocks with inferred series/axis labels. Alternatively, VLM-based chart data extraction (structured JSON output from a vision model) would bypass OCR entirely.

root_causes.root_cause: The 48% char-count accounting gap between meta flat_char_count (39,671) and audit-reported block text sum (20,634) is an audit measurement methodology error, NOT a code bug. flat_char_count is computed via _flat_block_primary_text() which correctly includes table row_records for role=table blocks. The audit's block text sum uses block.get('text','') which returns empty string for table blocks (they carry content in row_records, not text). The depth-1 flatness is a separate issue: Arabic legal documents without markdown-detectable heading markers produce flat trees because Docling's hierarchical postprocessor cannot recover structure from them.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/helpers.py:_flat_block_primary_text (line 2812) computes flat_char_count correctly; src/pageindex_mcp/client.py:1694 persists it
root_causes.suggested_fix: No code fix needed for the char-count gap -- the meta flat_char_count is correct. The audit methodology should use _flat_block_primary_text() (or sum row_records for table blocks) instead of block.get('text',''). The depth-1 Arabic legal doc flatness is the same Arabic heading recovery limitation seen across multiple Arabic documents.

root_causes.root_cause: Content-filename mismatch for ward 597 is a source-file-level data quality issue. The PDF file itself contains Decree-Law 42/2023 anti-commercial-fraud text despite being named about craftwork skills program. The pipeline correctly extracts what is IN the file -- doc_id is generated via uuid.uuid4() per file, filename is taken from os.path.basename(staging_key), and file_bytes are read from the staged MinIO object. No cross-assignment or file-swap occurs in the code path.
root_causes.code_path: src/pageindex_mcp/worker.py:process_document_job (line 395-404) binds filename; src/pageindex_mcp/converters_cli.py:main (line 129) passes to client.index
root_causes.suggested_fix: This is a corpus data quality issue: the source PDF was likely mislabeled or swapped before ingestion. A content-vs-filename consistency check (e.g. comparing extracted text keywords against filename tokens) could flag such mismatches post-ingestion, but the pipeline itself is working correctly.
